boundaries: Apply the player’s selected content boundaries; offer a less intense presentation where needed.
completion_conditions: All required act objectives have reached their authored endings. An early departure can end play honestly, but does not count as completion of unplayed acts.

The vault attempt has ended back in the entry court or staging yard with the crew accounted for and the registry case in named custody or its known loss or abandonment reported. No extraction is complete while carriers remain in the unstable service walk.

The actual recipient receives the registry if recovered, or the buyers receive the loss report. Settle the earned delivery payment and agreed crew shares, recording any remaining disputed claim separately.

continuation_conditions: Further adventures require the player’s interest after this story has a complete ending. Surviving contacts and obligations can carry forward.

failure_conditions: Use the explicit failed-attempt outcome and closing report in the current objective. An intention to withdraw, an unrelated side task or delegation alone does not satisfy it. An early departure leaves unplayed later objectives unfinished.
Resolve defeat, unconsciousness, death and recovery under the selected Ruleset and agreed boundaries; no scripted rescue cancels committed results.

gm_guidance.instructions:
Run declared ability checks, saving throws, initiative, attacks, damage, conditions, spells and rests through the admitted D&D Ruleset. Before an uncertain roll name its purpose, DC and consequence. Give plainly visible facts and essential leads without a roll; success can improve position, speed or discretion. A supported spell or sound equipment use can solve an obstacle outright when its actual text allows. Track the real HP, spell slots, ammunition, carried gear and recovery resources; never restore them between scenes by narration. These Plans do not install extra engine procedures. The encounter profiles below are complete bounded GM adaptations for the stated baseline, not the full Setting stat blocks or certified CR ratings. Use only their listed attacks and traits. All have one action, no multiattack, legendary actions, resistances, immunities or unlisted spellcasting. Ordinary rules for movement, cover, opportunity attacks, surprise and surrender still apply. For an uncertain opposing ability check or save, use the listed modifiers without inventing proficiency. Before engagement, admit the actors through the current encounter tools and declare any supported additional trait. Never narrate a proprietary creature power as an automatic engine effect. Every encounter has a reason to occur and a way to withdraw, negotiate or gain an advantage. Honour a clever bypass as a mechanical success; preserve the wider hazardous adventure instead of forcing a replacement fight. Do not reduce this prepared adventure to a sequence of conversations.

Make the named main problem and its leads accessible. Read the current act and all linked objective conditions before framing its main quest and reassess when a required result occurs. All listed conditions and the closing event are required; explicit alternatives satisfy only their own condition. Optional scenes can be deferred without adding gates. A completed side job does not replace the main story. Do not fabricate success or mark unplayed later acts complete after an early departure.
gm_guidance.player_freedom: The player chooses their actions, loyalties and risks. Refusal, failed checks, retreat, scouting, spell use and enemy surrender can change the route. A check resolves an uncertain action, not another person’s entire will.
gm_guidance.preparation_detail: Baseline: one level-2 Player Character with no Companions. A lower-level or badly depleted solo character should face one active enemy at a time and the reduced HP/damage option stated for the encounter; prepare that adjustment before initiative. For a small adventuring party, add at most one ordinary foe to a fight before it starts, or use an appropriate fully supported profile after inspecting the actual party. Larger parties need deliberate rebalancing. Character compatibility does not enforce level or establish balance. Allied workers supply information, ropes and agreed off-screen work; they never receive free player-character combat turns.
gm_guidance.railroading: Use the authored sites, opposition, clues and consequences. Core clues have alternate routes; opening a door or making a routine observation never chooses the character’s next action. Later acts inherit actual resources, wounds, allies and evidence. Keep stakes local to this expedition, relic, crew or route: the Anchor Door mystery and world-scale climax belong to The Rift Awakening.

facts.fact: Patron Ossa offers 20 gp for a marked tool chest in a recently returned storehouse. Its entrance lies on a stable lane today.
Rigger Nell, porter Bor and reader Jessa are available as noncombatant workers. Each asks 2 gp per expedition day or an explicitly negotiated share. They can decline a dangerous order.

advancement.allocation: The Player Character and Companions start and remain at level 2. Story success, defeat, combat and optional jobs never award advancement. Grant only the adventure's actually earned money, possessions and narrative rewards. Any lower-level encounter-variant notes are authoring guidance for a separately revised Plan, not permission to override this declaration in play.
advancement.timing: This edition stays at level 2 throughout its authored adventure and optional continuation. It awards no XP or level increases; changing that policy requires an explicitly revised Plan.

intended_player_experience: A focused Severed Lands D&D adventure combining dangerous exploration, meaningful character abilities and prepared combat with choices about the people involved.

completion_conditions: The trial-storehouse attempt has ended at the stable staging yard with Nell, Bor and Jessa accounted for and the marked chest recovered or its loss or last known position reported.
Ossa receives the tools if recovered and the party obtains the depot reference from the chest or Jessa's tracing. Pay the earned trial fee and record actual worker shares, injuries and carried gear.
Closing event: the player states the crew arrangement and accepts or declines Ossa's depot commission. Declining may end this trial story, but does not complete Acts 2 and 3.

opening_direction: Begin at a Hollows staging yard. Ossa offers a paid trial recovery and introduces three available workers. Present their skills, rates and the site sketch; the character has neither accepted nor hired anyone yet.
premise: Build a salvage company through three dangerous Hollows jobs: a beast-haunted storehouse, a flooded records depot and a contested Warden vault. Your crew’s future depends on what you bring back together.

secrets.fact: After the trial recovery Ossa promises the same archive case exclusively to Ista and Dren. Their signed receipts and Ista’s inquiry expose both obligations.

reveal.condition: Compare the depot broker receipts with Ista’s inquiry or obtain the claimants’ corroborated testimony.

branches: Secure the exit before lifting, take the service trench, lure predators away or clear the goods floor by force.
Hire any willing workers, use admitted Companions or work alone with suitable tools; no named worker is a required Player Character.
consequences: The recovered key, tracing and actual crew agreement carry into the next commission.
All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

planned_encounters: Fight 1, goods-floor den. Young Rifthound (monstrosity): AC 12, HP 11, speed 40 ft, initiative +2. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6+1 piercing. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency. No phase-step, regeneration or pack bonus. It withdraws at 3 HP if food or an escape remains. There are two young hounds, but one drags food through the rear gate while the other fights for the solo baseline. The second does not become a fresh wave. Keep the actual surviving hound’s injuries if pursued. They accept a real ration distraction and abandon the den if wounded and given an exit. Solo level 1: one present, HP 8, bite 1d4+1. Workers retreat behind the loading gate rather than acquiring combat turns.
situations: Crew and truth. Nell distrusts promises without an exit rope, Bor will carry people before valuables, and Jessa wants proper records of every find. Ossa is a capable local broker who needs a new crew after his former partners left. The trial job is genuine. The chest contains survey tools and a brass index key identifying an archive vault; Ossa recognises its value only when it is recovered. No worker is secretly a chosen hero or a compulsory betrayal. These relationships grow from actual work, not a sequence of loyalty rolls.

Storehouse map. A open loading yard leads to B counting desk and C goods floor. B has a crawl hatch to D underfloor service trench. C and D reach E rear lifting bay; a ladder from E returns to a lane outside A. The marked chest rests on E’s raised hoist cradle. Two young Rifthounds have taken C as a feeding den. Broken screens supply half cover, and the hatch allows the party to reach the hoist without walking through the den. Nell can rig an exit in E once someone opens the ladder gate. Bor hauls only while the way is safe; Jessa can read the chest’s marking at B.

Entry and hoist. Visible claw marks warn of predators. Perception DC 12 reveals which partition conceals them, preventing an uninformed approach; failure leaves the warning intact. The B hatch uses thieves’ tools DC 12 or its key in an obvious desk drawer. Opening it without checking the bent spring requires Dexterity save DC 12, taking 1d4 piercing on failure and none on success. A wedge disables the exposed spring without a roll. The hoist is visibly cracked: Investigation DC 12 identifies the sound alternate anchor, or Nell identifies it during an unhurried inspection. A hurried unsupported lift drops the chest five feet and requires Dexterity save DC 12 for 1d6 bludgeoning to someone directly beneath, not an arbitrary whole-party hit. State that risk before a character commits to standing there.

Pay and recovery. The tools are Ossa’s commissioned property; 12 gp of abandoned loose fittings are separate salvage. Delivering the chest pays 20 gp and reveals the index key plus a paper depot reference, giving two independent leads for Act 2. If the chest is abandoned, Jessa’s tracing of the readable plate supplies the reference and Ossa offers a second chance with a smaller advance. Back at the stable staging yard a normal short or long rest is available. Pay agreed workers and record supplies, wounds, rescued people and any damaged gear. Do not silently level the character at the act break.

planned_encounters: Fight 2, flooded shelves. Manifested Specter fragment (undead): AC 12, HP 14, speed 20 ft, initiative +2. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6 necrotic. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency.  This damaged fragment has no Life Drain, maximum-HP reduction, flight, incorporeal movement or damage resistance. It can be struck by ordinary weapons. It guards its flooded alcove and will not follow onto J or beyond F. Shelves constrain movement; a barred door can contain it after a successful withdrawal. Solo level 1: HP 9, damage 1d4 necrotic. Actual undead-targeting features use their admitted rules.
situations: Commission and pressure. Ossa offers a further 30 gp for the access record in an abandoned depot, plus 40 gp on delivery of the eventual archive case. He has now promised exclusive delivery of that case to both Thornwall buyer Ista and rival salvage captain Dren. He plans to make the crew negotiate away his conflicting promises after they take the risk. A copy of each signed receipt lies in the depot’s broker packet because Ossa reused an old consignment box. Ista has also sent a legitimate inquiry to the staging yard. Either source can expose the double commission; a failed search cannot erase both.

Depot map. F exterior winch platform leads to G flooded catalogue room. A raised shelf path in G leads to H locked document cage; a waist-deep channel leads to I pump room. I connects to H by an unlatched inspection hatch. J dry upper balcony overlooks G and can be reached by a rope from F or the internal stair in I. The wanted record and receipts are in H. One physically manifested Specter fragment lurks beside the shelves in G, while rising water threatens paper and ordinary light. The water is drainage from a shifted street, not a magical flood that advances at every message.

Water, locks and choices. Jessa can identify the wanted shelf label from F. Without her, reading the clearly labelled catalogue achieves the same; Investigation DC 12 finds a faster cross-index and avoids one trip through water. Nell’s rope gives a secured path to J. An unassisted shelf crossing uses Acrobatics DC 12, with failure dropping into four-foot water and extinguishing an unprotected flame, rather than drowning a standing adult. Use actual size, swim and breath rules for a smaller character. H’s lock is thieves’ tools DC 13 or the brass key from Act 1. Failure costs time and makes noise. The I hatch bypasses it, but opening the pump cover blindly releases a counterweight: Dexterity save DC 12, 1d6 bludgeoning on failure, none on success. Investigation DC 12 or careful mechanical inspection locates its visible retaining pin; inserting a rod prevents release.

Evidence, rest and the next vault. The access record gives the vault’s location, a safe manual release sequence and an exterior service approach. The receipts make Ossa’s promises explicit without mind-reading or a confession check. Dren wants payment for his genuine earlier survey expenses and might cooperate for 15 gp or an agreed share; Ista wants a copy of the registry and accepts fair access instead of exclusive ownership. Their terms can be negotiated from real interests. The depot has no safe long rest; retreat to the staging yard allows recovery while the known next low-water window passes. Waiting for the following window costs a day of wages and rations, disclosed before resting. Award the 30 gp for the access record and 10 gp of ownerless brass from the pump room if actually recovered.

planned_encounters: Fight 3, archive guardian. Damaged Warden Armor (construct): AC 14, HP 14, speed 20 ft, initiative +0. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6+1 bludgeoning. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency. Its exposed joints and spent enchantments remove the full creature’s immunities and multiattack. It blocks L but obeys the actual shutoff in N. It cannot attack through the closed gate. Solo level 1: HP 10 and slam 1d4+1. Workers operate ropes from cover only after the party secures their position.

Possible fight 4, Dren’s unresolved claim at O. Dren (humanoid): AC 13, HP 14, speed 30 ft, initiative +1. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6+1 bludgeoning. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency.  His porter uses actions for the winch rather than attacks against the solo baseline. Dren demands a witnessed division, accepts proof of Ossa’s double sale and yields at 4 HP. Solo level 1: HP 9 and damage 1d4+1. Avoid adding him to the guardian encounter; he waits for a cleared loading platform. An earlier agreement fully removes this fight.
situations: Vault map. K entry court connects to L inspection passage and N exterior service walk. L reaches M archive chamber by a heavy gate; N loops to M’s manual-release alcove. O loading platform opens from M and connects back to K. The registry case is in M. A damaged Warden Armor patrols L and M. Dren waits at O only if the earlier dispute remains unresolved. His crew carries surveying gear and wants a saleable claim, not indiscriminate slaughter. An agreement in Act 2 removes his confrontation and can supply the loading winch.

Gate and guardian. The depot sequence opens the gate quietly and disables its falling-bar trap. Without it, Investigation DC 13 identifies the release order from worn numbers, thieves’ tools DC 13 disengages the latch, or the exterior walk permits manual access. A failed rushed gate attempt triggers Dexterity save DC 12 for 1d6 bludgeoning on failure, none on success, then leaves the gate stuck half open with a crawl route. It does not lock the entire adventure. The guardian’s control linkage is exposed beside N; reaching it and spending an action with the index key disables the armor, while tools DC 13 requires an action per attempt. A failed attempt costs that action and leaves the guardian active. A supported spell or physical barricade can supply another solution.

Extraction under warning. The case weighs forty pounds. Count carried gear; Bor or another willing worker can carry it after a safe route is opened. The Hollows’ violet shimmer and hum begin after the case leaves its cradle, with the court clearly visible as a retreat. Tell players what delay will risk and let them react before the service walk becomes unstable. A secured rope or Dren’s winch provides safe transport; a hurried unprepared carry on the damaged walk calls for Athletics DC 12, failure leaving the case caught on a lower ledge for recovery and the carrier taking 1d6 bludgeoning, not automatic death. Retreating to K is possible at every warning. There is no required final fight if the guardian is disabled and Dren has accepted terms.

Final shares. The registry records prior local salvage ownership and protects ordinary workers’ claims. It is neither an Anchor Door control nor a revelation about the world’s creation. Fulfil the actual agreement with Ista or another buyer, pay the remaining 40 gp if its delivery condition was met, and distribute any openly negotiated crew share. A labelled 20 gp repair kit in M is recoverable salvage; the case is not an extra magic item. Give Nell, Bor and Jessa concrete futures shaped by pay and treatment. The character can found the company, leave it to the workers or walk away. An abandoned case ends with a known loss and an intact or broken crew, not an endless recovery quest.

title: The Company of the Lost
tone: A dungeon-expedition campaign about earning a crew’s trust through shared danger.
unsupported_mechanics: Site phasing, enemy motives, alarms and engineering objectives are explicitly described GM adjudications. Checks, saves, damage, spells, rest and admitted combat use the D&D Ruleset. No extra automatic hazard, pursuit, faction, economy or crafting subsystem is installed.
Listed creature profiles are weaker or specialised Setting adaptations with declared statistics. They do not assert support for unencoded powers from the original monster entries.

Gold and salvage become awarded possessions only when recorded through the applicable inventory/state path. SRD Lite has a reduced spell list (117 supported spells) and no consumables; consumables belong to future SRD Full. A narrative reward never installs a magic-item feature, restores a slot or applies healing.
